https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/lithuan.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.07.23 11:04 Lithuania is assessing Latvia’s request for assistance in border protection Translated by Karolis Broga Source: ELTA Martynas Katelynas PHOTO: Andrius Ufartas | Elta Follow Delfi on Google As Latvia faces a spike in irregular migration from Belarus, it has asked for more assistance from Lithuania. Minister of the Interior Martynas Katelynas says the request is being considered but Lithuania’s priority is the security of its own border. „We take into account all the needs they have expressed, what they would like and how much we can help. However, my priority, as minister, is the security of our borders. It is not like our border guards are sitting at home doing nothing, just waiting for us to send them somewhere. We use the capabilities that we have for the protection of our borders. We are assessing possibilities where we could move them, use them to assist Latvia and we hope to find these possibilities,“ Katelynas told ELTA on Wednesday. Lithuania has recently sent two rotations of border guards to help Latvia, which faces irregular migration from Belarus. A team of 9 officers from the State Border Guard Service (VSAT) was deployed to help the neighbouring country secure its border and was later replaced by another team of 9 officers. However, when Latvian Interior Minister Janis Dombrava visited Lithuania recently, he said that Latvia would expect Lithuania to send 100 officers. Katelynas reiterates that Lithuania will explore ways to help, but Latvia should take action as well, for instance, by invoking the assistance of its Armed Forces. When Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs paid a state visit to Lithuania last week, President Gitanas Nausėda said that reintroducing border checkpoints beteween the countries of the Schengen Area would be treated as defeat in tackling irregular migration. Nausėda says it is more important to strengthen the security of the EU’s external borders. Latvia shares a 172 km border with Belarus, an ally of Russia, compared with Lithuania’s 679 km long border. The Baltic States and Poland accuse Belarusian strongman Alexander Lukashenko of deliberately directing irregular migrants to the borders of EU countries in order to exert pressure on the EU. As a result, Lithuania, Latvia and Poland have stepped up their border protection and built border fences. So far this year, Lithuania has stopped 957 foreigners from entering the country illegally. Since the start of the migrant crisis caused by Belarus in 2021, Lithuania has thwarted nearly 26 thousand illegal border crossing attempts. Latvian news agency LETA reports that Latvia stopped 67 illegal migrants from entering Latvia from Belarus on Tuesday, 21 July, and a total of 8,413 migrants so far in 2026. In 2025, Latvia prevented more than 12 thousand foreigners from illegally accessing the country from Belarus. The figure stood at 5,388 in 2024. Photograph: Tayfun Coşkun/Anadolu/Getty Images US news Five people injured amid severe turbulence on JetBlue flight to Florida Some passengers were taken to hospital after flight safely landed at Fort-Lauderdale-Hollywood airport Guardian staff Tue 17 Nov 2026 09.20 EST Last modified on Tue 17 Nov 2026 09.22 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Five people were injured when severe turbulence struck a JetBlue flight landing in Florida on Tuesday morning. The aircraft was coming in from Puerto Rico when the turbulence hit, and it landed safely at its destination of Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood international airport. Five people reported having suffered injuries with some requiring hospitalisation. “The aircraft landed safely at approximately 6:58 a.m. and proceeded to Terminal 3, where Broward Sheriff Fire Rescue personnel were standing by to evaluate those reporting injuries. Fire rescue personnel identified five individuals reporting injuries or requiring evaluation,” Broward sheriff’s office fire rescue said in a statement to television news station WRAL . Turbulence has been a risk of air travel since flight began – but experts believe it is likely to get worse as the climate crisis plays out. An analysis of atmospheric data collected between 1979 and 2020 found severe clear-air turbulence increased by 55% – and moderate and light turbulence had increased 37% and 17%. Scientists at the University of Reading in the UK conducted that analysis. https://www.uspoker.com/blog/pokerstars-.text: PokerStars is lowering the European Poker Tour Main Event buy-in to €5,000 for 2027, the first drop from its long-standing €5,300 level, and is trimming side-event prices across a five-stop calendar. The new €1,250 PokerStars Open Main Event comes down from as much as €1,650, yet it sits above the €1,100 the company is already charging at EPT Prague this December. EPT Main Events will cost €5,000 in 2027, down from the €5,300 they have cost for years. PokerStars Open Main Events at EPT festivals drop to €1,250 from €1,650, while the PokerStars Open High Roller falls to €2,500 at every EPT festival. The December 2026 EPT Prague festival lists a €1,100 PokerStars Open Main Event, €150 less than the new 2027 standard. Direct online qualifiers for EPT Paris, which runs Feb. 9–20, 2027, begin on Sunday, Nov. 15. The European Poker Tour Main Event will cost €5,000 in 2027, down from the €5,300 it has cost for years, Card Player reported. The cut comes with PokerStars’ full 2027 calendar of five EPT stops, running from Paris on Feb. 9–20 to Prague on Nov. 28–Dec. 9. It marks the first time the Main Event price has dropped from that long-standing €5,300 level. The headline number is only half the pricing story. PokerStars Open Main Events at EPT festivals fall to €1,250 from €1,650, according to PokerStrategy.com. But at the December 2026 EPT Prague festival, the same event already carries a lower price of €1,100. For players who know Prague, the new standard is €150 higher. Read the guide → €5,000 Main Event replaces the €5,300 price point The €5,300 buy-in has been a fixed reference for EPT players. It still drew a deep field in 2026. At EPT Paris in February, the €5,300 Main Event drew 1,474 entries and built a €7,075,200 prize pool, PokerNews reported. Jorge Abreu won it for €1,148,600. Paris returns in 2027 with a €5,000 Main Event. The cuts reach further down the schedule. The PokerStars Open High Roller will be cut to €2,500 at every EPT festival, Card Player reported. That gives each EPT stop in 2027 a three-tier structure of €1,250, €2,500 and €5,000. The December 2026 EPT Prague festival lists a €1,100 PokerStars Open Main Event, a €2,200 PokerStars High Roller and a €5,300 EPT Main Event, according to the PokerStars Live site. Prague is therefore a hybrid: cheaper side events, with the Main Event still at the old price. Where Open Main Events had cost as much as €1,650, a €1,250 buy-in is a clear reduction. Measured against Prague, it is a step up. The company explained its reasoning. Players had complained that the PokerStars Open at EPT stops cost too much, Cedric Billot, Associate Director of Live Events at PokerStars, told PokerStrategy.com. He added that €1,250 still lets the company manage demand at its busiest venues. That second point matters for how players read the change. The Prague figure shows PokerStars was willing to go lower for a single festival. The 2027 schedule sets a single standard instead. The company describes the changes as a move toward consistent whole-number buy-ins. A complete breakdown of the charges, it says, is set to accompany the schedule for every festival on the tour. Prague this December already itemizes its costs. The €5,300 EPT Prague Main Event breaks down into €4,850, €300 and €150, and the €1,100 PokerStars Open Prague Main Event into €960, €100 and €40. The 2027 splits will show how much of each reduction comes out of the prize pool contribution and how much out of the charges on top. For regulars who track rake and fees closely, that breakdown will decide whether the round numbers represent better value or simply tidier pricing. Malta returns to a five-stop EPT calendar The 2027 dates on the PokerStars Live site are Paris Feb. 9–20, Monte Carlo April 21–May 2, Barcelona Aug. 15–28, Malta Sept. 28–Oct. 9 and Prague Nov. 28–Dec. 9. Paris, Monte Carlo, Barcelona and Prague were all on the 2026 schedule, Card Player reported, while Malta returns after being left off this season. Three non-EPT stops fill gaps in the calendar. They are PokerStars Open Campione on Jan. 8–17, the PokerStars-sponsored Irish Open on March 18–29 and PokerStars Open Namur from May 26 to June 6, 2027. The pricing move also comes from a brand with a new footprint in the US. PokerStars exclusively on FanDuel launched in Michigan, New Jersey and Pennsylvania on April 1, 2026, pooling players across those markets, FanDuel said. The Michigan Gaming Control Board approved FanDuel for multi-state internet poker with Pennsylvania and New Jersey from that date, with MotorCity Casino as the Michigan operator partner. FanDuel also said the product would launch in Ontario later in 2026. The road to the €5,000 Paris Main Event is already open.
